visual_metadata.social_alt: A mineral owner compares documents beside “How to Build a Property-Scope Crosswalk Before Comparing Mineral Rights Offers”.

findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 7f2e631f3e89874ec99900784a51f0690f3d7babeca185d27827dc093f06bbfe; all 6 declared sources passed current access review.

Claims remain bounded to official RRC and GLO search fields, the RRC GIS limitations, the defined Texas Property Code disclosure context, and current MRX package-index and price-per-net-mineral-acre boundaries. No source is converted into a private title, ownership, acreage, legal-description, value, fairness, contract, or transaction conclusion.

The article invents no real owner, property, buyer, contract, transaction, price range, production, reserves, forecast, testimonial, success rate, or owner-specific legal, tax, accounting, title, appraisal, engineering, investment, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Public GIS Viewer (Map) (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas Public GIS Viewer page identifies survey, lease-ID, and well searches and states that its GIS datasets are informational, approximate, non-authoritative, and may be unsuitable for legal, engineering, or surveying purposes.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the viewer only as a research lead for identifiers and repeats the RRC limitations. It does not use a map or dataset to establish ownership, title, acreage, legal-description identity, value, or the effect of an instrument.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Well Records (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas well-records page lists county, lease or well name and number, operator, field, Commission identifiers, and survey, abstract, section, and block as useful record-search details.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the list only to recognize fields that may appear in source documents or research leads. It does not treat regulatory records as proof of ownership, title, net mineral acres, legal scope, value, or transaction terms.

sources_inspected.label: Texas General Land Office, Land Grant Database (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas General Land Office Land Grant Database provides search fields for county, abstract number, original grantee, part section, and survey, block, or township.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those fields only to help readers recognize and preserve stated location identifiers. It does not use a land-grant result to determine current ownership, title, acreage, legal equivalence, value, or whether an offer is complete.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Legislature, Property Code Chapter 5, Subchapter F (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Chapter 5, Subchapter F includes a disclosure rule for a defined category of mailed mineral- or royalty-interest purchase offer, and the statutory notice refers to the description of the property being conveyed.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses only that bounded observation to explain why the stated property description deserves a separate comparison field. It does not decide whether any communication is covered, compliant, enforceable, void, sufficient, or otherwise legally effective.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, How to Build a Mineral Rights Sale Document Package Index (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX document-package guide owns file identity, page and attachment inventory, package completeness, version control, and source-location recording.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article links to that guide only as the prerequisite file-organization boundary. It does not repeat the package-index workflow and instead begins with field-by-field transcription of the property and interest scope stated inside the organized files.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, How to Calculate Price per Net Mineral Acre From a Mineral Rights Offer (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX price-per-net-mineral-acre guide requires the price numerator and acreage denominator to refer to the same property and interest scope and stops the calculation when scopes differ.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article links to that guide only to mark the next-step boundary. It does not calculate price per net mineral acre, infer acreage, compare economics, judge fairness, or recommend an offer.
